explain.say: Aphra Behn said she saw these events herself, in the English colony of Surinam in South America in the 1660s. Her short novel Oroonoko, published in 1688, tells of an African prince sold into slavery. A gentle warning: it describes slavery and cruel violence. The panels tell his story.

explain.say: Look at the third panel. An English captain invites Oroonoko aboard his ship as a friend, then chains him and sells him in Surinam, where he is renamed Caesar. There he finds his beloved Imoinda, also enslaved. What does the captain's trick say about the colonists?

explain.say: The fifth panel. Promised freedom again and again, Oroonoko leads the enslaved people in a revolt, but they are betrayed. Rather than let Imoinda and their unborn child live in slavery, the two choose her death together. He is executed with terrible cruelty, without crying out. Why does Behn make him so calm?

explain.say: Is it an anti-slavery book? On the left, it shows slavery's cruelty and a noble African hero, and later abolitionists read it. On the right, Oroonoko himself sells captives, and the book mourns betrayed kings more than it attacks slavery. Which side does the evidence support?

right.title: Royalist romance
points: Hero is a prince, not everyman

explain.say: Behn lived in the Restoration, after 1660, when the king returned and theatres reopened, and women acted on stage for the first time. She was one of the first English women to earn her living by writing. Wonderful. Challenge: compare her narrator's claims to be an eyewitness with Crusoe's.

faq.a: An African prince, Oroonoko, is tricked into slavery and taken to Surinam, where he is reunited with his love Imoinda, leads a failed revolt and is brutally executed.
Critics debate it. It shows the cruelty of slavery and a heroic African, but it focuses on a noble prince, Oroonoko trades in captives himself, and it never calls for ending slavery.
An English playwright, poet, novelist and one-time royal spy, who lived from about 1640 to 1689 and was among the first English women to earn a living by writing.
The return of the monarchy under Charles the Second in 1660, after the Civil War and Commonwealth. Theatres reopened, actresses appeared, and witty, often bawdy comedy flourished.

faq.q: Why is Behn important for women writers?
faq.a: She proved a woman could write professionally for money and fame. Virginia Woolf later said all women ought to honour her, because she earned them the right to speak their minds.

facts: English theatres, closed in 1642, reopened at the Restoration in 1660.
Aphra Behn was buried in Westminster Abbey in 1689.
